## Four changes up (2607, 2608, 2609); AC2 patch applied; a new defective-AC class identified

2607 (c379 childless-story veto): plan review PASS, seven ACs met. The AC6 defect-seeded RED is the
sharp part -- restoring the branch failed the story case while the [task], [bug] and [epic]
parameterizations STAYED GREEN. That asymmetry IS the defect, and the parameterized oracle now pins
it rather than pinning the story case alone. One forced deviation from the stated fix shape: deleting
only the four veto lines left 'skipped_needs_planning = []' with no remaining append, so mypy lost
the element type and typecheck failed ('Need type annotation'). An explicit list[tuple[str, str]]
annotation is the minimal repair. Blast radius 436 passed / 0 failed across 16 files.

2608 (ae97 AC4 detector): PASS on the third gate run, claimed, pushed.

  A DEFECTIVE-AC CLASS WORTH NAMING, and the best catch of the batch. AC4 originally required
  observing both findings ON THIS HOST -- but AC1 REMOVES the stalled condition. The moment AC1
  lands, AC4 becomes unrunnable. This is the same family as the time-dependent ACs the operator ruled
  out earlier: an acceptance criterion whose verifiability depends on state THE FIX ITSELF DESTROYS.
  'Wait 24h and observe no flap' and 'observe the stall that AC1 removes' fail for the same reason --
  the proof is not reproducible on demand. Remedy applied: re-anchor the proof to unit tests driving
  both signals against a synthetic state dir and a throwaway git repo, and DEMOTE the live-host
  reading to a one-time recorded datum (reject-streak 122, build-stale 201 on 2026-09-03). Now
  order-independent. Generalization for future ACs: if landing an earlier AC would make a later one
  unverifiable, the later one is defective as written.

  Gate economics worth knowing: run 1 BLOCKED in 6 SECONDS with NO LLM SPEND -- the deterministic
  floor (P1 readiness-shape, P10 verification-presence) short-circuits before any model call. So a
  structurally malformed plan costs nothing to bounce. Only run 2 (5.6 min) and run 3 (6.1 min) were
  billable. Fixing all advisories in ONE pass rather than across two runs was the right economic call.

  The description cap was the binding constraint exactly as expected: P4 reported 7556/8000, leaving
  444 chars -- nowhere near enough for a checklist plus a Testing section. Moving forensics to a
  comment took it to 4367.

  ADVISORY RECORDED, NOT ACTIONED: build_drift.detect_drift performs NO FETCH, so origin/main is
  whatever the checkout last fetched. A rarely-fetched laptop UNDERSTATES drift. That is the
  conservative direction -- it can never invent drift -- and is documented at TRACKED_REF, so it was
  left. Real limit worth knowing.

  Also: that agent deliberately used the worktree CLI rather than the MCP server for tracker writes,
  reasoning that the MCP server runs the 201-commit-stale global build, so using it to write a ticket
  whose gate verdict you then trust is the exact failure mode being fixed. Correct call. Note the
  consequence: the on-box MCP server keeps serving stale gate code to EVERY session until AC1/AC2
  land.

2609 (S6 bounded gate admission): PASS on the sixth pass, five BLOCKs each of which improved the
design. Default cap 4, derived not guessed: 4 x ~748 MB ~= 2.99 GB fits the ~3 GiB left on the
t4g.large after ~2.17 GB steady state and Gerrit's ~3 GiB reservation; a fifth run (~3.74 GB) does
not. Counter is flock'd slot files in the snapshot store's EXISTING locks/ dir -- cross-process and
crash-safe without a heartbeat, because the kernel drops a flock when the holder dies. That matters:
it delivers the property the PID+heartbeat lease was supposed to, without reviving the design ADR
0112 records as rejected-as-unsound. Degradation splits by fault: missing fcntl or one bad slot file
ADMITS AND ANNOUNCES; an unreachable store root REFUSES, because otherwise the scratch volume's
failure mode is silently reverting gate bytes to the root filesystem -- which is the outage this
epic exists to prevent.

  It also found a real latent bug while testing: _cli/_llm_commands._review_plan hardcodes 'return 1'
  for an LLMError where its sibling calls _llm_error_exit_code. Caught by an AC test going RED at
  'assert 1 == 11'.

  SYSTEMIC FINDING WORTH WATCHING: the plan reviewer blocked twice on prerequisite-consistency
  because it compares against the ADR draft PINNED ON PREREQUISITE 7dfa (three decisions) while
  merged origin/main has seven. A review pins its dependencies' material at review time, so a
  prerequisite that lands and grows leaves dependents being judged against the stale copy. Worked
  around by citing decisions BY HEADING rather than by number. This is the fourth instance of the
  propagation meta-pattern.

AC2 PATCH APPLIED to ~/.local/bin/rebar-dev-update.sh with operator approval. Original backed up to
rebar-dev-update.sh.pre-ac97.bak. Applied with patch(1) -- git apply refused because the diff names
orig.sh/new.sh, being harness-generated. bash -n clean; the UV_BIN hardcode at :18 is now UV_BIN=""
with selection at :190. Updater running once now to confirm it publishes a current build.
